draft_abstract: We study the aligned timelike scalar principal block of P(X,Y)=P0(X)+Z(X)Y. First, whenever X>0, Y>0, Z_X is nonzero, and the kinetic and gradient matrices are positive definite, the exact identity det(K-G)=-4XYZ_X^2 forces the generalized scalar speeds to satisfy 0<c_-^2<1<c_+^2. Thus no choice of P0 can make both active scalar modes subluminal relative to the metric cone. Second, writing u=beta X^2 and q=d ln Z/d ln u, nonnegative active mixing over [u0,U] implies the strict bound U/u0<[1+1/(4q0)]^4. The two results respectively constrain the characteristic cones and dynamic range of derivative-gated two-scalar models. They are local architecture-specific design obstructions, not an unconditional causal or full-action no-go theorem.
